=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/persist_budget.py:328 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The last run added `and failed(items[-1])` to `if len(items) >= limits["max_rounds"] and failed(items[-1]):`, so the rounds cap fires only when the newest round failed; review rounds are always journalled with `--outcome ok` (scripts/review_commit_changes.sh:705-709) and no acceptance field, so review rounds can never trip `max_rounds`.
  WHY: With PERSIST_BUDGET_ENABLED=true, an issue cycling through review/autofix rounds goes past PERSIST_MAX_ROUNDS (default 5) and keeps getting `continue within_budget`; only the 48h `max_hours` cap still bounds it. This contradicts the plan's unconditional rule (docs/plans/persistent-unattended-workflows-plan.md:482). The tests hide the gap: they use review entries with outcome "fail", which production never writes, and `max_rounds_with_passing_newest_round_continues` asserts the narrowed behaviour. All four reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/persist_budget.py:316-320 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `max_hours` measures elapsed time from `oldest = parse_ts(ordered[0]["ts"])`, the first journal entry ever written, and a governor `blocked` escalation counts as final only while it is the newest entry, so a resumed issue (or a stranded `governor/ok` re-plan) past PERSIST_MAX_HOURS is escalated again with `escalate max_hours`.
  WHY: Every time a person removes `ai:needs-human` to resume, the issue is pushed back to `ai:needs-human` on the first idle tick, with another label edit, another `## Persistence budget reached` comment and another `stage=governor` entry. Unattended work cannot resume without editing the journal by hand. All four reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/persist_budget.py:86-88, 343-346 (also ~71 per minimax, 177-179 per gemini) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `OPEN_PR_LABELS` (`ai:done`, `ai:review-blocked`, `ai:ready-to-merge`) is label-based and leaves out `ai:implementing`, but plan.yml's "Skip when issue already has a PR" gate (.github/workflows/plan.yml:1007-1105) is PR-based and ignores labels. An issue with an open PR that still carries `ai:implementing` (for example, the best-effort relabel at .github/workflows/implement.yml:6722-6723 failed) therefore gets `replan`.
  WHY: The poller moves the issue to `ai:planning` and posts `/answer`; plan.yml then skips because the PR is open, and later ticks return `already_decided` (persist_budget.py:321-322). The issue stays parked in `ai:planning` until `max_hours` escalates it. All four reviewers rated it MAJOR.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19632-19638 (callers ~23108-23112, 30730-30733) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The comments-cache guard in `persist_budget_govern_issue` treats an authoritative empty cache (length 0) as unusable and runs a paginated `gh api` comments fetch for every candidate before any decision; the managed caller maps both "available and empty" and "unavailable" to `[]`.
  WHY: The tick cap (lines 19621-19624) limits only acting decisions, not reads, so API calls per tick grow linearly with the number of candidates and can exceed the plan's budget of "about 30 calls per poller tick" (plan:699). Severity disagreement: gemini and luna rated it MAJOR, minimax and glm rated it NIT; the highest is used.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19722-19744 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: When posting the escalation comment fails, the failure is only logged (`|| echo "...reason=comment_post_failed..."`), and the `governor blocked` journal entry is still appended unconditionally.
  WHY: Later ticks return `already_decided` because of the newest governor/blocked entry (persist_budget.py:316-317), so the `## Persistence budget reached` comment, the only place the reason and summary reach a human, is never retried. The label is still applied. All reviewers rated it NIT.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:~19610 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `pbg_label` and `pbg_edit_args` are declared at function scope in `persist_budget_govern_issue` but used only in the replan branch, which triggers ShellCheck SC2034.
  WHY: This is a lint failure with no runtime defect, but it blocks the shellcheck pre-push job, which the gate lists as failed.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:30723-30727 (vs 23064) | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: A comment claims the managed dedicated-phase skip list matches the standalone skip list, but the managed list includes `ai:security-pass` and `ai:security-pass-fixing` and the standalone list (line 23064) does not.
  WHY: Behaviour is the same today because `decide` ignores any label containing "security", but the false invariant lets the two lists drift silently.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Rounds on the current approach are at least PERSIST_MAX_ROUNDS, or there were PERSIST_REPLAN_AFTER_FAILED_ROUNDS consecutive failed rounds, or 2 consecutive no-progress failed rounds: re-plan if approaches are below PERSIST_MAX_APPROACHES, else escalate." (docs/plans/persistent-unattended-workflows-plan.md:482), with the linked issue's "Implement exactly what the plan assigns to phase P6 ... do not shrink P6's scope."
  expected_change_site: scripts/persist_budget.py `decide()` (max_rounds trigger at line 328; open-PR escalation branch at lines 343-346) and its table-driven tests in tests/test_persist_budget.py
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: `max_rounds` now also requires `failed(items[-1])` (scripts/persist_budget.py:328-329), which review rounds never produce; the added test `max_rounds_with_passing_newest_round_continues` (tests/test_persist_budget.py:122-124) locks in the narrowed behaviour; any trigger on an issue labelled ai:done/ai:review-blocked/ai:ready-to-merge becomes `escalate open_pr:<trigger>` even while approaches are below the cap; no hunk amends the plan or records an approved deviation, which is described only in the agents.d fragment, the changelog and the editor's PR comment.
- requirement: "API: at most 2 writes per decision. Decisions are capped at 5 per tick." (docs/plans/persistent-unattended-workflows-plan.md:497)
  expected_change_site: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh `persist_budget_govern_issue` (replan and escalate paths) and the standalone state-write call site around line 23113-23119
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: A standalone re-plan makes up to 4 writes: label edit (19699-19704), `/answer` comment (19711-19712), journal append (19735-19744) and state comment (23113-23119). An escalation makes 3: label (19722), comment (19728-19730) and journal append. agents.d/8427-p6-persist-budget.md documents the overrun, but no hunk restores the 2-write limit. The extra writes are bounded by the 5-decision tick cap.
- requirement: "Stay inside the files the plan lists for P6", the `files_touched` grant (ai:pipeline-plan-grant:v1) on linked issue #8561
  expected_change_site: .github/workflows/ci.yml (line 672) and docs/INVENTORY.md (line 190)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: Both files are in pr_changed_files.txt and match no files_touched entry. They were edited because tests/test_ci_wires_every_test_file.py and tests/inventory_parity.py require new tests and scripts to be registered. The pre-push gate lists tests/test_files_touched_scope_guard.py as a failure caused by this change. The editor disclosed the deviation, and the defect may sit in the plan-phase grant. Severity varied: gemini, minimax and luna rated it BLOCKER, glm MAJOR, sonnet NIT.
- requirement: "Switch-off byte identity" tests compare affected behavior with fixtures captured from `main`.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_orchestrate_poll_process.py and tests/test_persist_budget.py
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The tests cover the helper's disabled mode and statically check that the poller hooks are guarded, but they do not run the poller with the switch off and compare its behaviour against a pre-change fixture.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

  PROBLEM: The rounds cap fires only when the newest round failed; the review stage always writes `--outcome ok` with no acceptance argument (attempt_journal.cmd_append stores it as given, scripts/attempt_journal.py:613), so review rounds can never trip `max_rounds`.
  WHY: The issue goes past PERSIST_MAX_ROUNDS and keeps getting `continue within_budget`; only `max_hours` bounds it. This contradicts plan P6 check 2 (docs/plans/persistent-unattended-workflows-plan.md:482). The tests use review entries with outcome "fail", which production never writes. Fix: restore the unconditional cap.
- scripts/persist_budget.py:lines 316-319 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: A governor escalation counts as final only while it is the newest entry, and elapsed time is measured from the first entry, so a resumed issue returns `escalate max_hours` again.
  WHY: Every resumption is re-escalated, with another label edit, comment and governor entry, so work cannot resume without editing the journal by hand. Fix: measure from the first entry after the newest governor/blocked entry.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:lines 19728-19731 | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: If posting the escalation comment fails, the governor still appends `governor blocked`; the next tick returns `already_decided`, so the comment is never retried.
  WHY: The human never sees the reason or summary; the label is still applied.
